subject.title: Centralize chat-session naming; define subagent session lifetime & cross-channel persistence

question: Which Gateway-owned session identity and lifecycle contract should OpenClaw use for agent-created ACP/subagent sessions?
rationale: Current main has several valid partial mechanisms, and choosing the canonical owner and precedence order affects persisted session metadata, UI display, ACP cleanup, and cross-channel behavior.

options.title: Centralize title and lifecycle in Gateway
options.body: Make the Gateway session store the canonical source for display title and ACP/subagent lifetime, with derived titles and transcript session_info only feeding that contract.

options.title: Document the current split
options.body: Keep dashboard titles, derived titles, ACP bindings, and subagent archive semantics separate, and close only the documentation gap.

options.title: Design a broader persistent identity schema
options.body: Introduce explicit cross-channel agent/session identity metadata and migration rules before changing naming or cleanup behavior.

recommendation.title: Centralize title and lifecycle in Gateway
recommendation.body: Make the Gateway session store the canonical source for display title and ACP/subagent lifetime, with derived titles and transcript session_info only feeding that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the recent generated-title and title-precedence work and is the strongest current-main routing signal for the Gateway/session contract.
